speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your hypertension, have you noticed any headaches, blurred vision, or abdominal pain recently? REQUEST TEST: Basic metabolic panel, electrolytes, and urinalysis.

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Born full term with an uneventful neonatal period. Social history: Patient attends kindergarten. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco smoke.

speaker: Patient
text: All systems review is essentially negative as reported by the mother. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the mother reports no focal neurologic or abdominal symptoms, have your blood pressure readings been consistently elevated in both arms and over the past few weeks? REQUEST TEST: Renal_ultrasound and Echocardiogram.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Echocardiogram shows narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation; left ventricular function is normal. Renal ultrasound: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta.

The echocardiogram confirms a narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, which is the classic presentation for coarctation of the aorta in a pediatric patient with systemic hypertension. The normal renal ultrasound and lack of abdominal or visual symptoms rule out renal parenchymal disease and malignant hypertension from other causes. I will now finalize this diagnosis based on the definitive imaging findings.
